task.name: A role whose output is only usable when structured is assigned to a model that cannot produce it, so the gate depending on that output presents no recommendation and cannot say why
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2378
---

**Depends on #2378.** The assignment guard this issue asks for has to consult whether a model has demonstrated it can return a structured result. #2378 is what produces that fact, by exercising the capability and reporting per-capability outcomes instead of a single pass. Without it there is no recorded answer to "can this model return a structured artifact," and this guard would have to re-derive the answer at assignment time or assume it — which is the assumption that caused the failure described here.

## Observed

A story reached the escalate gate. The gate ran its advisor, the advisor produced output, and the
gate then presented its full set of operator actions with no recommendation attached and no
indication that the advisory step had failed rather than declined.

The advisor had been assigned to a model whose transport rejected the structured tool-call request.
The run fell back to plain text, which cannot carry the structured report the gate requires, so
report validation failed and the gate recorded the advisory as unavailable. The advisory step
consumed wall clock and spend and returned nothing usable.

Because there was no recommendation, the expiry path had nothing to apply and preserved the
checkpoint for an operator instead. The story had already been marked failed by then, so the
preserved decision was for work no longer running.

The model carried an explicit eligibility restriction in project configuration naming the phases it
was allowed to serve. That restriction did not prevent this assignment, because the advisor role is
not one of the phases the restriction vocabulary can express.

## Expected

A role whose result is only usable as a structured artifact is assigned only to a model able to
produce that artifact. Where no eligible model can, the role reports that it could not run, and the
step that depends on it states that its input is missing rather than presenting a degraded result as
a complete one. A step that produces nothing usable is not silently indistinguishable from a step
that ran and had nothing to say.

Eligibility declared for a model governs every role that model can be assigned. Where a role sits
outside the vocabulary those declarations use, it is nameable in that vocabulary, so a restriction an
operator writes cannot be silently narrower than the set of jobs the model will actually be given.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** The escalate gate offered its operator actions with no advisory recommendation, and the
advisory-unavailable state was reached through a failure rather than an absence of opinion.

**Evidence.**

- `src/theforge/config/model_identity.py:79` — `KNOWN_PHASES` is `frozenset({"preflight", "dev",
  "plan", "review"})`. The advisor role is not a member, so it cannot appear in a
  `routing.phase_eligibility` list.
- `src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py:303` — parsed phases are rejected when outside
  `KNOWN_PHASES`, so an operator cannot name the advisor role even deliberately.
- Run log, escalate gate on one story: the advisor start line, then a transport error on the
  tool-call request and a fallback to single-shot text mode, then
  `advisory report failed validation: ['no <advisory_report> block found in advisor output']`.
- The resulting pending record carries `advisory_unavailable: true` alongside the full options list.

**Ruled out.** Not the advisor prompt: the advisor was reached and produced output. Not the report
validator: it correctly rejected text with no report block. Not the expiry path, which behaved as
specified — it had no recommendation to apply. Not operator configuration error: the restriction the
operator wrote was accepted by config validation and simply does not reach this role.

**Confirmed cause.** Advisor assignment draws from the eligible model set without requiring the
capability its output format depends on, and the eligibility vocabulary cannot express the advisor
role, so neither the automatic path nor an operator override can keep an unsuitable model out of it.

**Affected code path.** Advisor model selection, the tool-call-to-text fallback in the transport
layer, and advisory report validation at the escalate gate.

**Fix-success criterion.** A model that cannot produce the advisor's structured output is not given
the advisor role; when the role cannot be filled, the gate states that the advisory is missing and
why, and that state is distinguishable from an advisor that ran and returned no recommendation.

handoff.summary: Implemented advisor as a first-class phase-eligible role guarded by recorded structured-output capability evidence. Added persisted provider-capability records from `forge check-providers`, used them in escalation advisor selection to fail closed before launch when no advisor-eligible model has demonstrated `tool-structured` support, and threaded explicit advisory-unavailable reasons through pending-gate rendering, resume persistence, and audit surfaces. Updated config/readiness/coordinator seam tests accordingly and verified the tree with `make dev-check`.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] Advisor assignment is now phase-eligible, gated on recorded structured-output capability evidence, and surfaced to operators as explicit missing-input states with seam coverage for the observed failure mode. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Capability gating and the advisor-unavailable taxonomy are well built, but stamping phase='advisor' on the runtime profile flips API-transport runners into review-submit mode, and readiness statuses that mean 'capability demonstrated, cost unknown' are recorded as not-demonstrated, which blocks the advisor permanently on CLI setups. (Verified HEAD 02abc0c0 matches the authoritative gate commit; authoritative verdict PASS — the dev handoff's 'BLOCKED' claim was not used.)

findings.description: The advisor profile is now stamped with phase 'advisor' instead of inheriting 'preflight', and on API transports the runner classifies every phase outside preflight/dev as a review phase, so the advisor is handed submit_review tools and a code-review forced-output contract even though its only usable output is a plain-text advisory_report block, which the report parser then rejects.

Persisted capability records copy the readiness attempt status verbatim, so an attempt that returned a valid structured verdict but could not report CLI cost is stored as unverified and read back as not-demonstrated, and the advisor is then refused at every escalation for a model that visibly produced the required structured artifact.

Every failure to select an advisor profile is recorded as no_structured_capable_model, including the distinct cases where no configured model declares advisor eligibility and where the profile's model identity could not be resolved at all, so the machine-readable reason misdescribes two states whose repairs differ.

Two new public helpers, phase_candidates and select_preflight_like_candidate, are added but never called anywhere in the source tree or tests, and phase_candidates duplicates the existing private _phase_candidates used by derive_roles.

With no capability store present the advisor refuses to run for every existing project until an operator runs forge check-providers, and no documentation or runbook change in this commit tells the operator that this new manual, cost bearing step is now a precondition for advisory output.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 requires '#2378's recorded per-capability result,' but no such coordinator-queryable record exists. src/theforge/cli/provider_readiness.py:199 returns an in-memory ReadinessResult, and src/theforge/cli/providers.py:33-114 only prints those results. ForgeConfig contains no readiness evidence. Moreover, advisor probes are stamped as phase='preflight' in _stamp_phase(), so _requires_structured_verdict() does not require a structured payload for that probe. The plan's own mitigation says to block when this API is absent; that condition currently holds, so the structured-capability acceptance criteria cannot be implemented without re-probing or assuming capability.
  Suggestion: Extend or amend the dependency to persist and expose an authoritative result keyed by canonical model identity, transport, and the exact structured-output capability, then name that public query/helper in Step 2. Rebase this issue after that contract lands.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 does not enumerate the state and caller surfaces needed for a durable machine-readable unavailable reason. CoordinatorState currently has only advisory_launch_failure/advisory_launch_reason; resume_persistence.py and audit.py serialize only those fields, while review_phase.py consumes the AdvisoryReport-or-None result. Restricting changes to the listed Step 3 files risks making the reason visible only in the immediate pending record.
  Suggestion: Specify whether the reason travels in a richer return value or new CoordinatorState fields, and include coordinator/state.py plus the applicable review_phase.py, resume_persistence.py, and audit.py callers/serialization tests.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 and the plan's own second risk mitigation state opposite rules for the unknown-capability case. Step 2: 'If no eligible model has demonstrated that capability, do not call run_agent.' Risk 2 mitigation: 'Fail closed only when explicit eligibility or structured-output evidence excludes the model.' Absence of evidence is the normal state — a fresh project, or any model never exercised, has no recorded outcome — so under Step 2's reading the advisor is disabled everywhere by default (today it always runs via config.preflight_profile at escalation_advisor_flow.py:247), while under the risk mitigation's reading a model that has never been probed is still given the role, which is exactly the failure this story exists to prevent. A dev agent cannot safely pick; the choice determines whether AC1 holds or whether the escalate gate loses its advisor entirely.
  Suggestion: Settle the tri-state in the plan: recorded-capable → assign; recorded-incapable → exclude; no record → state explicitly which way it resolves and why (e.g. fall back to the existing declared/probeable signal rather than to silence). If unknown resolves to 'do not assign', say what the gate reports and add a Step 4 test that an unprobed model yields a stated missing-input reason rather than a silent advisor-off.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 1 (the #2378 per-capability structured-output record may not be available) is unretired and lands on the surface AC1 depends on. Verified in this checkout: src/theforge/model_profiles.py aggregates per-model/per-role dev run outcomes only, with no structured-output capability bucket; the only structured-output evidence anywhere is cli/provider_readiness.py's READINESS_CAPABILITY_TOOL_STRUCTURED probe (line 47, already including an 'advisor' probe at build_readiness_probes), which is an on-demand CLI check, not persisted data readable at assignment time. The plan's mitigation — 'block this issue rather than re-probing' — is an instruction to not implement, not a retirement, so Step 2 has no verified data source.
  Suggestion: Name the concrete seam Step 2 reads (module + accessor + returned shape) as delivered by #2378, and state the behavior when that accessor returns no entry for the selected model. If the accessor may be absent at dev time, specify the fallback evidence source explicitly (e.g. the provider_readiness tool-structured probe result) so the guard is implementable against something that exists.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's file list is short of the surface it must touch. Advisor is not a role in RoleAssignment — bridge.py:112 derives only preflight_profile, and escalation_advisor_flow.py:247 does replace(config.preflight_profile, ...). The eligibility filter is _phase_candidates in config/role_derivation.py (line 111), which Step 2 does not list, and ModelProfile (config/types.py:348-390) carries no phase_eligibility field, so the coordinator cannot check advisor eligibility from the profile it holds without a registry lookup.
  Suggestion: Add config/role_derivation.py to Step 2 and specify the lookup path from a ModelProfile back to its AgentSpec/ModelInfo routing (registry key or model id) so the phase='advisor' filter is actually reachable from run_escalation_advisor().
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 does not say whether 'advisor' also joins _DEFAULT_PHASE_ELIGIBILITY (model_identity.py:145), which is a separate frozenset from KNOWN_PHASES (line 167). If it is not added, every model without an explicit list becomes advisor-ineligible and _phase_candidates' empty-set fallback silently restores the whole pool — the exact invisible failure mode the comment at model_identity.py:158-163 warns about. If it is added, existing explicit lists such as models.yaml:111 [preflight, review] will exclude advisor, which is the intended behavior but a live behavior change for current configs.
  Suggestion: State the choice in Step 1 and add a test for each side: a model with no phase_eligibility remains advisor-eligible (or not, per the choice), and a model with an explicit list that omits advisor is excluded without the empty-set fallback re-admitting it.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 3 (transport fallback not surfaced to coordinator code) is largely retired but not exactly for the observed failure. AgentResult already carries transport_fallback_fired / transport_fallback_reason / transport_used (agent_types.py:110-113), so a reason can be threaded; however the observed defect was a tool-call request rejected and downgraded to plain-text single-shot inside run_api_agent (runners/api.py:1146-1148), which is not the cli→api transport fallback those fields record.
  Suggestion: In Step 3, derive the 'structured request degraded' reason from the runner signal that actually fires for the tool-loop→single-shot downgrade, or classify it validation-side (report block absent while tools were requested) rather than assuming transport_fallback_fired covers it.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
